rows.currentScript: Start with minute and hour. Many minutes make one hour, a bigger unit. So hours make one day, bigger again. Clock and week miss that step in size.
rows.whyRewrite: Rule stated does not exclude the distractor week: "Many minutes make one hour, a bigger unit. So hours make one day, bigger again." Many hours also make a week, which is bigger again. The script must name the NEXT unit up (60 minutes to an hour, 24 hours to a day) for "Clock and week miss that step in size" to follow.

rows.currentScript: Read captain and ship first. A captain steers the ship he leads. So a pilot steers a plane, and plane fits. Airport and wing sit by planes, steering nothing.
rows.whyRewrite: "Airport and wing sit by planes, steering nothing." describes wing wrongly: a wing is part of a plane, not beside it. Also "A captain steers the ship he leads" assumes a captain is male.

rows.currentScript: Take the pair bee and honey. A bee gives honey to eat. Milk is what a cow gives. Farm and grass go with cows, not food.
rows.whyRewrite: "Farm and grass go with cows, not food." is false for grass: grass is food (the cow's food). The contrast needs to be "not what a cow gives".

rows.currentScript: First read sheep and lamb. A lamb is the baby of a sheep. Likewise a foal is the baby of a horse. Stable and hay go with horses, not young.
rows.whyRewrite: "Stable and hay go with horses, not young." is clipped and ungrammatical; a child can read "not young" as describing the horses. Needs e.g. "not with their babies."

rows.currentScript: Look at spider and web. A spider builds a web to live in. A bird builds a nest to live in. Egg and branch sit by the home, not it.
rows.whyRewrite: "Egg and branch sit by the home, not it." is clipped ("not it") and misdescribes egg, which sits in the nest, not by it.

rows.currentScript: Read foot and shoe first. A shoe covers the foot warmly. A hat sits on the head. Hair and neck sit by the head, covering nothing.
rows.whyRewrite: "Hair and neck sit by the head, covering nothing." is false for hair, which grows on the head and covers it. "A shoe covers the foot warmly" adds a claim the link does not use.

rows.currentScript: Start with kitten and cat. A kitten is a young cat. In the same way, a puppy grows into a dog. Bone and kennel go with dogs, not grown up.
rows.whyRewrite: "Bone and kennel go with dogs, not grown up." is ungrammatical and unclear to a child. The link also shifts wording ("is a young cat" then "grows into a dog"), so the same sentence is not carried across.

rows.currentScript: Read bird and nest first. A bird lives in a nest, its home. A bee lives in a hive, its home. Honey and sting come from bees, not homes.
rows.whyRewrite: "Honey and sting come from bees, not homes." reads as "honey does not come from homes", but honey is made in the hive. Misleading description of a wrong option.
